title: Resource Throttling Governance and Release Coordination
summary: Cross-functional coordination on throttling governance for the upcoming inference feature launch. Decided baseline CPU/GPU and request-level throttles, fallback routing priorities, and a phased release gate tied to telemetry checks. Assigned owners for telemetry dashboards, canary plan, and an incident runbook update.
action_items: Marta: Build per-route throttling prototype in staging and share perf numbers (due 2026-03-18)
Jonah: Draft policy doc for resource governance (include burst vs sustained rules) (due 2026-03-15)
Ethan: Add KV-cache hit-rate and prefix-latency graphs to the release dashboard (due 2026-03-12)
Carlos: Update oncall playbook with throttling escalation steps and run a tabletop (due 2026-03-22)
Priya: Finalize phased canary cadence and communicate to partners (due 2026-03-14)
next_steps: Share initial perf spreadsheet and gating criteria with execs by 2026-03-11
Schedule a 30-min canary dry run next Wednesday and invite SRE oncall
Lock down the OSS onboarding checklist (licenses, tests, quantization profiles)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-09 14:00 UTC | Duration: 75m | Attendees: Priya, Jonah, Marta, Ethan, Carlos, Leah

[00:00] Priya: alright uh thanks everyone for being on time, i know this is a heavy one. objective today is to align on throttling governance and release gating for the inference feature roll. we're tight on schedule so we'll keep to the agenda.
[00:32] Jonah: cool, i'll start with where runtime is at — we've got the continuous batching tuned for the new model, but we still see tail latency spikes when prefix cache misses align with high concurrency. the kv cache eviction is slightly aggressive when token windows are big.
[01:05] Marta: yeah that was visible in the incident last week, we hit a cascade where kv evictions plus a sudden burst caused nodes to pile up requests — we had queuing and then the scheduler started dropping lower-priority traffic.
[01:28] Ethan: to add, the kernel fallback path also adds ~80ms on median for those sequences, so when we hit fallback it compounds. we should probably set a throttling threshold at the front-door so we don't cascade into kernel fallback frequently.
[01:52] Priya: question for reliability — do we want per-route throttles or global request shaping? tradeoffs?
[02:15] Carlos: per-route is more precise but harder to reason about. global shaping reduces complexity but can block critical low-latency routes. my recommendation: layered approach — route-level nominal limits, plus a global safety net.
[02:40] Marta: agree. and include categories: interactive chat low-latency, batch embedding medium-latency, background rerank best-effort. set different burst budgets.
[03:05] Leah: (interrupting) also need to think about billing signals — we don't want customers to be surprised when throttling reduces token consumption. can we tie throttle logs to billing notes?
[03:30] Jonah: yeah we can add a throttle_reason field in responses and surface to billing later, but initially keep it in telemetry only.
[03:48] Priya: ok noted. next — release gating. i propose three gates: perf verification in staging, canary to 5% traffic with gating metrics, then ramp to 25/50. gating metrics are p95 latency, error rate, kv-cache hit ratio, and cost-per-token delta.
[04:18] Carlos: add oncall-alert-signal — if total SLO burn rate > 2x baseline for 10 minutes, immediate rollback.
[04:40] Marta: we should define exact thresholds, e.g., p95 increase > 40ms over baseline or error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m.
[05:02] Ethan: note that when we quantize models for cost we also see slightly different memory patterns, so host saturation could look different — include GPU util and OOM rate in the dashboard.
[05:28] Priya: good. OSS onboarding — what's the status on the model licensing checklist?
[05:45] Jonah: OSS team has the initial list. outstanding items: official quant profiles, unit/regression tests for tokenization edge cases, and a small inference benchmark harness that runs nightly.
[06:08] Marta: we also need to ensure audit logs capture model pinning and who changed runtime flags — audit is required for private deployments. I noticed the current audit stream misses some kernel selection changes.
[06:33] Carlos: right, and KMS integration for private customers is a different conversation, but for the launch we just need to ensure key actions are logged.
[06:50] Priya: sounds like action items: telemetry updates, policy doc draft, throttling prototype. we'll capture ownership after this.
[07:10] Leah: quick question — competitors like Cumulus AI have a per-tenant quota model with burst credits, should we borrow that idea?
[07:30] Jonah: burst credits help smoothing but are hard to reason about when you have multi-tenant oversubscription. I'd rather we do explicit burst windows with decay.
[07:50] Marta: agreed. and for fairness use a weighted token budget per customer tier.
[08:10] Priya: ok, next — incident retro follow-ups. Marta, can you summarize what we learned?
[08:25] Marta: summary: root cause was an interaction between aggressive KV eviction and scheduler bumping lower-priority requests; mitigations we applied were increased cache TTL, temporary throttling on experimental routes, and a fast rollback of the new kernel fallback. actionable learning: we need canary limits for kernel fallback rollouts and observable hooks to detect prefix-cache churn.
[08:58] Ethan: small point — the fallback detection currently uses a heuristic that reports after 30s; we should tighten that to 10s for the next rollout.
[09:18] Carlos: and add an SLO guardrail in the scheduler that pre-emptively re-routes to a cheaper model variant if latency goes above X.
[09:36] Jonah: concern: rerouting to cheaper variant can cause quality regressions. we need a quality monitor tied to a prompt set so we can detect regressions quickly.
[09:55] Priya: yes, include a small canary prompt set and pass/fail thresholds. we have Redwood Optimize historically, but sometimes the name is messy in docs — people call it the Optimizer. we should standardize naming.
[10:20] (brief side conversation about naming consistency)
[10:40] Leah: timeline check — we have a feature freeze in two sprints (around 2026-03-20). to ship we need gating docs and a green canary by then.
[11:00] Priya: so let's target perf numbers in staging by 2026-03-12, policy doc by 2026-03-15, and a canary window week of 2026-03-22.
[11:18] Marta: on the perf numbers — i will spin up a staging job that simulates 10k concurrent requests with mixed-route traffic and capture p50/p95/p99 and kv hit curves.
[11:35] Jonah: i'll help with the harness and ensure kernels used in staging match prod kernels — we've seen mismatches in the past where staging used an older kernel.
[11:50] Ethan: note about observability retention — for debugging we want 14 days of high-resolution prefix traces but that's costly. propose 7 days high-res and 30 days low-res.
[12:12] Carlos: SRE supports that compromise, but we should have an on-demand snapshot option for 30-day window for postmortems.
[12:30] Priya: good. security/compliance point — Leah, anything on audit or SOC/ISO that we should consider?
[12:45] Leah: SOC2 control: change approvals must be recorded and reviewable. ensure release doc includes signatures for kernel changes and throttling policy. for private deployments, KMS usage must be verified before GA.
[13:05] Priya: thanks. discussion — canaries: how long should each canary phase be?
[13:20] Jonah: I'd do 2h observation for initial 5% then 12h for 25% and 24-48h at 50% depending on signals.
[13:40] Marta: make sure the canary includes synthetic traffic that exercises long prefixes and embedding routes.
[13:55] Ethan: also schedule a targeted load run during the 25% canary to validate auto-scaling behavior.
[14:10] Priya: ok, we need a clear rollback plan in the runbook — fast rollback automation for config flips and model pin reversion.
[14:28] Carlos: automation exists but we'll validate in a dry run next week. I'll add that to the action items.
[14:45] Priya: any other risks?
[14:55] Jonah: risk: cross-tenant noisy neighbor when a single tenant uses massive parallel batch jobs — need tenant-level isolation or pre-scheduling.
[15:12] Marta: mitigation: enforce per-tenant maximum concurrency and a job queue for large batches — and route batch jobs to dedicated capacity during peak.
[15:32] Leah: let's confirm messaging to customers if we throttle them — need a docs PR that explains the behavior and shows examples.
[15:48] Priya: who will own the docs PR?
[15:55] Leah: i'll own docs PR but need a tech reviewer — Jonah?
[16:05] Jonah: yep i'll review.
[16:10] (short tangential note about a procurement call later)
[16:25] Priya: ok quick recap of decisions: layered throttling (route + global), explicit gating metrics, canary cadence as discussed, telemetry updates to dashboard, update oncall playbook. action owners in notes.
[16:48] Marta: i'll run the staging load and post numbers; if p95 stays within 25ms of baseline we consider staging perf green.
[17:00] Priya: final — schedule the dry run canary for next Wednesday 09:00 UTC, Leah will invite oncall and partners.
[17:12] Carlos: noted.
[17:20] Priya: thank you all. meeting adjourned.

References and links mentioned: perf spreadsheet (link: /doc/perf-throttling-sims), release gating doc draft (link: /doc/release-gating-draft), canary runbook (link: /doc/canary-runbook).

End of transcript.
